_comment: I0 provider playbook (schema: app/domain/playbook.py). Public facts only, every claim sourced. SWFT / Bridgers publishes no law-enforcement channel and no freeze or AML policy: swft.le stays null. The only published address is a general 'contact' alias (not a catalogue local part, so it is declared with value null). Swaps settle in minutes: a hold is realistic only before payout, and a refund goes back to the sender's refund address (funds moved, not recovery).
notes: Operator: Explorerx Digital Limited; no governing jurisdiction or registration place is stated, so LE cooperation is likely cross-border. Not an issuer: when the payout leg was USDT or USDC, ask the issuer to freeze in parallel. The Bridgers API exposes refundReason 4 'Blacklisted' and 8 'Interact with risky address' and the status wait_for_information ('please contact customer service'): holds and refunds exist technically, but a refund returns funds to the depositor's refund address, which may be the scammer. Once paid out, follow the payout leg on-chain to the next custodian or issuer.

entities.name: Explorerx Digital Limited (SWFT Blockchain / Bridgers)
entities.notes: No jurisdiction is stated in the user agreement and privacy policy.

channels.label: General contact (support, complaints, data protection)
channels.notes: The only e-mail address in the privacy policy, also named in SWFT's own posts; a 'contact' alias, which the catalogue does not take as a value: add it as a case channel after checking the policy page. Telegram support (t.me/bridgers_cs) and live chat on swft.pro are the other user channels. Have the orderId ready.

swft.le.notes: No law-enforcement address, portal or AML policy is published: leave null until a source is found. Disclosure is made only when required by law, legal procedure or compulsory government authorities, so an officer writes to the general contact citing the orderId.

instrument.notes: A courtesy request; cite the police / IC3 reference.

paths.notes: Ask for a risk-control hold on an in-flight order (before payout) and preservation of the order records (orderId, deposit / receive / refund hashes, from and to addresses, device id, IP). No process is documented: any action is discretionary. 30 days is the privacy policy's reply time for complaints; there is no fraud SLA. Say plainly that a refund to the depositor's address would return the funds to the scammer.

instrument.notes: A police request citing the orderId; the operator's jurisdiction is not stated.

paths.notes: Undocumented: no LE process or freeze policy is published. Cross-border cooperation is likely needed.

instrument.notes: The privacy policy shares information when required by law, legal procedures, litigation or compulsory government authorities, and without consent where directly related to a criminal investigation.
